pages.title: How it works
pages.text: The apiary simulates a Productive Bees hive without placing bee entities. Each bee slot checks its own matching flower or pollen and writes products to the output area and fluid tank. One idle bee never blocks the others.

pages.title: Tiers and slots
pages.text: The basic apiary has 3 bee slots and a 9-slot output area. Basic/Advanced/Elite/Ultimate factories have 5/10/15/20 bee slots and split the output area over two pages. Optional addons register even higher tiers.

pages.title: Reading the picture
pages.text: The red slot on the left is the cage input, the blue slot on the right is the cage output, and each middle slot holds one bee with its model and status lamp drawn inside. Below is the output area; factories show "< 1/2 >" paging underneath.

pages.title: Bee tooltips
pages.text: Left-clicking a bee slot selects it and highlights the slot. Hovering shows name, age, health, progress, state and nectar; hold Shift to add flower requirement, productivity, endurance, temper, behaviour and weather tolerance.

pages.title: Gene treat feeding
pages.text: Gene sample + honey treat = gene-carrying treat. Feed it to a bee to rewrite the matching trait. Two methods: $(li)$(bold)Right-click a bee slot$() with the treat on your cursor to feed that one bee; $(li)$(bold)Drop the treat into the cage input slot$() and let the machine pick.

pages.title: How the machine picks
pages.text: Automatic feeding ranks bees by need: $(li)$(bold)Selected a slot$() (left-click for a highlight) → only that bee is fed; $(li)$(bold)No selection$()→ scan all bees, feed the one with the largest shortfall across the treat's genes. $(br2)Example: insert a treat with Productivity: very high + Weather tolerance: any + Behaviour: metaturnal, and the machine starts with low-productivity, rain-shy, day-only bees.

pages.title: No waste
pages.text: $(li)Trait already matches or beats the treat → $(bold)no consumption$(); $(li)Temper runs the other way, only pushes bees $(bold)towards passive$(); $(li)0% purity genes do not count (purity is success chance); $(li)Treats carrying a bee type gene are rejected—PB does not apply genes from those anyway; $(li)At most one bee per second, to avoid factory lag.

pages.title: Automating the supply
pages.text: The cage input slot is a standard input slot, so $(bold)pipes, hoppers and AE2 can all insert treats$(). Treats and cages share the slot safely: the machine checks for treats first each tick and only falls through to cage handling otherwise. Pair it with the gene sampler upgrade for a closed breeding loop: sample → craft → feed.

pages.title: The two toggles
pages.text: Conversion: once on, convertible items in the feeder are consumed and turned into products; it is off by default, so items act as flowers only and are never eaten. Disable mode: left-click to enter per-slot disable editing (the letter turns orange), then left-click a slot to disable or restore it. Outside the mode, Alt + left-click does the same. Shift-click the toggle to disable or enable all.

pages.title: Feeder stats panel
pages.text: The right panel shows slot usage, Active/Idle, the page number and the inserted flowers; with disabled slots the header becomes "Flowers (N disabled)". The bottom hint line changes with the state, reading either "Items are not consumed" or "Conversion ON: ingredients will be consumed".

pages.title: Factory tiers
pages.text: Each tier upgrades from the previous one and keeps the bees and installed upgrades inside. Do not look at speed alone: the faster combs pile up, the more the centrifuge, chests and network must keep up.

pages.title: Apiary-only switches
pages.text: On the Items page of side configuration these 14x14 buttons show a green letter when on: A = AE output, M = direct AE output, O = direct container output, D = centrifuge direct link, P = centrifuge priority (full centrifuges buffer inside the apiary and only overflow goes to AE). A/M/P exist only with AE2 installed.

pages.title: When it stalls
pages.text: No progress: check FE, bees and flowers (including disabled slots). Progress completes but nothing appears: the output area or fluid tank is full. Only some bees idle: hover each slot to see what it lacks. An upgrade will not install: check the machine type and the limit. A treat will not enter: only treats $(bold)carrying genes$() are accepted. Treat sits without being consumed: no bee currently benefits from those genes.
